tagline: Connect Jira engineering tickets to Salesforce cases and opportunities
metaTitle: Jira Salesforce Integration: Cases to Bugs and Back
metaDescription: Turn Salesforce cases into Jira bug tickets and close cases when the fix ships. GAIA ranks bugs by account revenue. See the setup steps.
intro:
Enterprise software companies run their customer relationships in Salesforce and their engineering operations in Jira. When a customer reports a critical bug or requests a feature, the information must travel from the CRM to the tracker for engineering action — and back when the fix ships. Without automation, that journey is manual, slow, and unreliable.

GAIA connects the two so customer-facing teams always know the status of the engineering work that affects their accounts. Salesforce cases escalated as bugs auto-generate Jira tickets. Ticket resolutions update case statuses. High-value opportunities with engineering dependencies surface their ticket status directly on the opportunity record.

For enterprise B2B SaaS companies where customer trust depends on reliable communication about engineering timelines, this integration ensures every customer-affecting issue is tracked end-to-end across both systems.

useCases.title: Salesforce case to Jira bug ticket
useCases.description: When a Salesforce case is escalated as a product defect, GAIA creates a bug ticket with the case description, account tier, ARR at risk, and a link back to the case for full customer context.

useCases.title: Jira resolution to Salesforce case closure
useCases.description: When a Jira ticket linked to a case is resolved, GAIA updates the case status and creates an activity for the account owner to notify the customer that their issue has been fixed.

useCases.title: Revenue-weighted priority
useCases.description: GAIA enriches tickets created from cases with the linked account's ARR and opportunity value, giving engineering a revenue-weighted backlog view for enterprise customer issues.

useCases.title: Deal-blocking issue escalation
useCases.description: When an opportunity is marked as blocked by a technical issue, GAIA escalates the linked ticket to Blocker priority and notifies the engineering lead, ensuring deal timelines are protected.

useCases.title: Quarterly business review readiness
useCases.description: GAIA generates a summary of all tickets linked to an account and their current status, giving customer success managers a complete engineering history before QBR calls.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Salesforce to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your Jira instance and Salesforce org in GAIA's settings. GAIA uses Connected App OAuth and API tokens, scoped to the minimum permissions your workflows require.
Define which case categories or opportunity stages trigger ticket creation, how case fields map to issue fields, and which ticket transitions write back to the CRM.
GAIA monitors both sides and executes your workflows continuously, ensuring cases become tickets promptly and resolutions reach the case records without manual intervention.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with Salesforce Service Cloud as well as Sales Cloud?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA integrates with both Sales Cloud (opportunities and accounts) and Service Cloud (cases and entitlements). You can configure workflows for each object type independently.

faqs.question: Can GAIA prioritize Jira tickets by account tier?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA reads the account tier or custom priority fields and maps them to ticket priority levels. Enterprise or Platinum tier accounts can automatically generate Blocker-priority tickets.

faqs.question: How does GAIA handle cases that don't require engineering action?
faqs.answer: GAIA only creates tickets for cases that match your configured criteria — specific case categories, escalation flags, or custom field values. Non-engineering cases are ignored.

faqs.question: Can I see ticket status inside the CRM without switching tools?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA writes ticket status back to a custom field on the linked case or opportunity, so account managers see live engineering status directly in the CRM without a separate login.
